title: Ashyan bar Nidbakh or Nidbah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was Rav Yeiva’s son-in-law, as in [Bava Batra 22b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.22b.7), and spoke in the name of Rav Yehudah in [Menachot 29a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.29a.18). The [Rif](https://www.sefaria.org/Rif_Halakhot_Ketanot_(Menachot).4a.3) and [Rosh](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_on_Menachot%2C_Hilchot_Sefer_Torah.15.1), in the laws of Torah scrolls and mezuzah, read that he spoke in the name of Rav, as does Dikdukei Soferim on Menachot there. In [Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 1:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Megillah.1.9.9), folio 11a, Rabbi Zeira speaks in his name; there the patronym is bar Nidbah.[^2]

notes.text: The ending says the name there is bar Nidbah, not that Zeira reports a second sage of that name. The complete Megillah 1:9 paragraph places the relevant teaching in the 11a section.

Bava Batra identifies Yeiva as Ashyan’s father-in-law. There Yeiva is the one who speaks in the name of Rav. In Menachot, Ashyan speaks in the name of Rav Yehudah. The Rif also reads Rav in its [mezuzah passage](https://www.sefaria.org/Rif_Halakhot_Ketanot_(Menachot).4b.8). In the Yerushalmi, Rabbi Yonah and Rabbi Yose transmit Rabbi Zeira’s citation of Ashyan bar Nidbah. Heilprin discusses these sources in the entries for [Ashyan](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=652&lang=en) and [Yeiva](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1614&lang=en).
